newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE COFFEE ENDS MIXED, SEPT/NOV STILL DISCOUNT.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE COFFEE ENDS MIXED, SEPT/NOV STILL DISCOUNT.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures were unimpressed with the gyrations of the New York market and opted to focus on spread deals after September failed to breach resistance at $1,675, traders said on Wednesday.

The nearby Sept/Nov spread attracted most interest with the discount widening at one point to around $10 from $3 earlier in the day. Traders said Sept/Nov started on Tuesday at a premium of around $8.
"It's been a premium board for a while and suddenly Sept/Nov is finding itself at a discount," said one.
"That's maybe a reflection of people's impression that there's enough coffee for September in London, which you don't have in New York," he said.
Market sources said the spread discount was capable of widening to as much as $16 but was still likely to find its way to being a premium.
The London market still had good availability of hedgeable robusta coffee, they said.
Supply was ample due to coffees which did not re-grade under the exchange's new criteria, in effect from the July delivery period.
But more liquidity was still needed in the further forwards to encourage higher volume from nearby October which could be rolled.
September closed down $11 at $1,645 after hitting its head on a band of resistance around $1,675. November was down $5 at $1,650 in a total market volume of 3,497 lots.
"It struggles into the resistance area we've got now, $1,675 basis September, and can't get through -- it's going nowhere," one trader said.
Despite the low seasonal demand from roasters, market sources said there was still limited trade buying under current prices to support the nearby contract.
